6. Against the Counter statement, the Claimant has filed a rejoinder stating that authorities holding the 
substantive and regular post of DGM (P&A) and GM (P&A) can exercise their disciplinary powers. Therefore, all 
proceedings conducted by 2"! Party Management are bad in law, ultra vires. It is a case of audi alteram partem and 
contrary to doctrine of natural justice and therefore, impugned order is required to be quashed with the benefit of 
reinstatement with back wages and all consequential benefits. 


7. Heard both the parties and gone through the materials and evidences placed on record. The first point for 
determination is whether the inquiry was conducted in a fair manner following the due process. Shri A.Pandiaraj, 
DGM In-charge (CMM) was appointed as enquiry officer. He framed the charge sheet and same was served on the 
delinquent employee. The petition never declined to receive the copy of charge sheet. On the contrary, he stated that 
he was not able to respond to the charge sheet and due to stress and mental illness. This is caused due to some 
matrimonial dispute. It appears that this explanation of the petitioner is a product of an afterthought for not the real 
cause of responding to the charge sheet. 


8. The counter affidavit filed by Shri Angel Sumith N., on behalf of the management clearly explained the 
conduct of the Petitioner. Mr.R.Senthil Kumar was an unauthorized absentee from 7.0.20l6 to 7.04.20l6 (3 
months). The management has sent a letter (Annexure No.|) and requested him to join duty. On 5.05.207, the 
Petitioner Shri R.Senthil Kumar submitted his resignation (Annexure No.2). This resignation explained the attitude 
of the petitioner that he was not ready to work with the Respondent. 


9. After receiving resignation, the management again sent a call back letter dated 4.06.20!7 (Annexure No.3) 
and Petitioner seeking excuse as mentioned by him (Annexure No.4). The management issued warning letter to the 
petitioner dated 05.07.20l7 (Annexure No.5). But, the Petitioner remained absent. At another occasions, he was 
served with notices (Annexure No.6 & 8). But considering no change in the behavior of the petitioner, the 
Disciplinary Authority decided to issue charge sheet to him and a copy was served to him (Annexure No.9) and the 
petitioner refused to collect to receive copy of charge sheet and it was returned to the sender with the remark, 
“addressee refused” (Annexure No.l0). The copy of the charge sheet was pasted on the notice board of the 
Department in the presence of the witnesses (Annexure No.|]). But no response was given by the Petitioner. The 
Disciplinary Authority appointed the Presenting Officer on 2.0!.20l9 (Annexure No.|2). A copy of this letter was 
sent to the Petitioner, but he refused to take the copy of this letter (Annexure No.|3). A copy of this notice was 
pasted on the notice board of the Department in presence of witnesses (Annexure No. |4). 


0. The Enquiry Officer again issued inquiry notice dated 9.03.20l9 (Annexure No.|5), but the Petitioner 
refused to take this notice (Annexure No.l6). A copy of this notice was pasted on the notice board of the Department 
in the presence of witnesses (Annexure No.|7). 


ll. The Enquiry Officer fixed another date for enquiry vide notice dated 04.04.20I9 (Annexure No.8), but the 
Petitioner refused to take this notice also (Annexure No.!9). A copy of this notice was pasted on the notice board of 
the Department in the presence of two witnesses. One more chance was given to the Petitioner by the Enquiry 
Officer and notice dated 23.04.20l9 (Annexure No.2l) was sent and the Petitioner was called for enquiry on 
03.05.209 at .00 am in his office. This notice was received and acknowledged by the Petitioner (Annexure 
No.22). Meanwhile, the Petitioner submitted his resignation vide letter dated 5.04.20l9 (Annexure No.54). 
Although, he stated that this resignation was not acceptable during the pendency of enquiry and he was advised to 
appear before the enquiry committee. But, the Petitioner never appeared before the enquiry committee and never 
responded the charges leveled against him. 


2. Therefore, in my view, the enquiry was conducted in a fair manner with transparency and in adherence to 
principles of natural justice. The petitioner was provided with several opportunities to explain the allegations. He 
was allowed to present the case and to present evidences, but the delinquent employee got himself absent from the 
enquiry proceedings. 


3. The second point for determination is whether charges which were framed against the delinquent employee 
were established? The management clearly mentioned the willful absence period of the employee, which is 
mentioned in para no.3 of this judgement. The petitioner never explained his position how he remained absent for 
the above mentioned period. The total number of absence of 289 days significantly impact on the respondent’s work 
place, leading to reduce productivity, increase workload for remaining employees, lowering morale and potential / 
financial losses and also disrupted work flow. Therefore, finding of the Enquiry Officer is absolutely perfect and no 
interference requires by this Tribunal. All charges mentioned hereinabove [in page 2 - a, b, c & d | are proved against 
the claimant. 


4. The third question for determination arises as to whether punishment of dismissal from service is shockingly 
disproportionate. As per the discussion above, the conduct of the workman/employee was improper. He adopted 
improper behaviour and violated company policy / standing orders. The petitioner disrupted the workplace and 
created negative impact. Therefore, I am of the view that termination of the petitioner from service is not shockingly 
disproportionate punishment, creating hostile or refusing to follow reasonable and lawful instructions from his 
superiors and in absentia from service for long period (292 days) are sufficient reasons to impose maximum penalty 
of termination from service. 


[भाग ए---खण्ड 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मार्च 28, 2026/चैत्र 7, 948 2057 


5. The Petitioner in his written argument submits that he has taken medical treatment and a certificate was 
issued by psychiatric and obtained medical fitness certificate dated 04.03.2020. But, this medical certificate never 
describe the course of treatment and this certificate does not state the mental disturbance as claimed by the 
Petitioner. 


6. The claimant raised another legal question in his rejoinder, although not claimed in the main petition, that 
Enquiry Officer was not authorized to conduct enquiry, because he was holding substantial and regular post of DGM 
(P&A) and G.M (P&A) cannot exercise the discretionary powers. Therefore, all proceedings conducted by the II 
Party/Management are bad in law and ultra virus. The designation of the Enquiry Officer is DGM (P&A) In-charge 
(CMM). The Enquiry Officer in the Departmental inquiry is appointed by the Disciplinary Authority, who should be 
a disinterested and impartial officer, preferably of a higher rank than the charged officer. Such Enquiry Officer 
should not be personally involved in the matter, as a witness or complainant. The claimant never alleges any bias 
against the Enquiry Officer. Therefore, Enquiry Officer was competent to conduct the enquiry against the delinquent 
employee. 


7. In the case of Kanhaiyalal Agrawal & Others Vs. Factory Manager, Gwalior Sugar Company Limited, AIR 
(200l) SC 3645, the Hon’ble Apex Court laid down test for loss of confidence to find out as to whether there was 
bonafide loss of confidence in the employee, observing that — 


“loss of confidence cannot be subjective, based upon the mind of the Management. Objective facts which would lead 
to a definite inference of apprehension in the mind of the Management regarding trustworthiness or reliability of the 
employee must be alleged and proved.” 


In the case in hand, the workman has absented himself unauthorisedly, failed to respond before the Enquiry Officer, 
created a false defense of mental disturbance, submitted his resignation during the enquiry, which resulted a hostile 
attitude of the claimant and such hostile attitude from an employee can manifest as negativity, resistance to feed back 
and difficulty in working with others, ultimately impacting upon productivity. 


8. As per the discussion above, I am of the view that Petitioner’s dismissal from service is justified and 
proper procedure was followed by the Enquiry Officer. Hence, the punishment imposed by the Management is just 
and proper and the claim of the Petitioner is rejected. 


9. In the result, the claim of the Petitioner is dismissed. 

An Award is passed accordingly.

l. In this case, an application under Section 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure, !908 on behalf of respondent 


no.l was filed for dropping the proceedings against it. It is maintained in the application that vide order dated 
03.06.2024, Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Allahabad Bench, Prayagraj (hereinafter called as Hon'ble 
NCLT, Allahabad) has appointed Resolution Professional (RP) of the respondent no.l company in case titled as ICICI 
Bank Ltd. V/s Jaiprakash Associates Ltd. In the said case, Hon'ble NCLT, Allahabad has passed following 
observations:- 


“02. As a necessary consequence of the moratorium in terms of Section 74, the following prohibitions are 
imposed, which must be followed by all and sundry:

a. the institution of suits or continuation of pending suits or proceedings against the corporate debtor 
including execution of any judgment, decree or order in any court of law, tribunal, arbitration 
panel or other authority; 


b. Transferring, encumbering, alienating or disposing of by the corporate debtor any of its assets or 
any legal right or beneficial interest therein; 


C. Any action to foreclose, recover or enforce any security interest created by the corporate debtor in 
respect of its property including any action under the Securitization and Reconstruction of 
Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002; 


d. The recovery of any property by an owner or lessor, where such property is occupied by or in the 
possession of the corporate debtor. 


८. It is further directed that the supply of essential goods or services to the corporate debtor as may be 
specified, shall not be terminated or suspended or interrupted during the moratorium period. 


f The provisions of Section /4(3) shall, however, not apply to such transactions as may be notified by 
the Central Government in consultation with any financial sector regulator and to a surety in a 
contract of guarantee to a corporate debtor. 


g. The order of moratorium shall have effect from the date of this order till completion of the 
corporate insolvency resolution process or until this Bench approves the resolution plan under sub- 
section (7) of Section 37 or passes an order for liquidation of the corporate debtor under Section 33 
as the case may be." 


2. In view of the above, AR for respondent no.| contended that all the proceedings pending before any Tribunal 
cannot go on against respondent no.| and he prayed that reference my kindly be dropped in the interest of 
justice. 

3. On the other hand, AR for workman on 26.09.2025 made the following statement: 


“Stated that I have received the copy of the application filed on behalf of respondent no.I under Section 57 
of the Code of Civil Procedure, /980 for dropping the proceedings against it and I do not want to file any 
reply to the same and will argue on the application orally.”’ 


4. AR for workman argued orally that in this case, Jaypee Cement Company have been bought by Ultratech 
vide tripartite agreement dated 29.06.20l7. He further referred to para 3 of the tripartite agreement executed by and 
between Jaypee Cement and Ultra Tech Cement, vide which Ultratech Cement company had agreed that it shall 
bound and liable for all the liabilities, obligations and to run the project on the terms and conditions as specified in the 
MOUs dated 09.07.2024, 8.08.20l0. He thus contended that he should be allowed to implead Ultratech Cement as 
party as it has taken over all the liability as per tripartite agreement dated 29.06.207. 


5. I have given due consideration to the arguments advanced by AR for both the parties. 


6. The present claim has been filed by the workman under Section 2A of the Industrial Dispute Act, 947 
(hereinafter called as ID Act) and now the worker wants to replace Jaypee Cement with Ultratech Cement Ltd. in 
view of the tripartite agreement executed between it and Ultratech Cement Ltd. dated 29.06.20l7. However, in this 
regard, it is pointed out that ICICI Bank has gone before the Hon'ble NCLT, Allahabad for liquidation of Jaypee 
Cement and Hon'ble NCLT, Allahabad vide order dated 03.06.2024 in the above mentioned case, had stayed all the 
proceedings before any Tribunal as per para l02 of judgment of Hon'ble NCLT, Allahabad as reproduced above. Now 
the effect of tripartite agreement would be seen by the Hon'ble NCLT, Allahabad while disposing of the petition of 
ICICI Bank. Since all the proceedings have been stayed by Hon'ble NCLT, Allahabad as per para 02 as reproduced 
above of its order dated 03.06.2024 and it would be a futile exercise to proceed further with the present case as all the 
proceedings before this Tribunal has already been stayed by the Hon'ble NCLT, Allahabad. 


Ts In view of this, the application is allowed and claim petition bearing ID No.l43 of 2024 is dismissed. 
Workman Sh. Malkiat Singh can proceed further before Hon'ble NCLT, Allahabad as per law. 


8. Let copy of this award be sent to the Appropriate Government as required under Section |7 of the Act for 
publication. File after completion be consigned to the record room.

I. कार्यक्षेत्र 


समिति का कार्य संविधान, राजभाषा अधिनियम एवं नियमों में राजभाषा के संबंध में दिए गए उपबंधों, केंद्रीय हिन्दी समिति के निर्णयों 
और राजभाषा विभाग द्वारा जारी किए गए निर्देशों/अनुदेशों के कार्यान्वयन के बारे में तथा विदेश मंत्रालय के कामकाज में हिन्दी के प्रगामी प्रयोग 
को बढ़ाने के बारे में सलाह देना होगा। 


IL. कार्यकाल 

इस समिति का कार्यकाल समिति के गठन की तारीख से, निम्नलिखित बातों के अध्यधीन सामान्यतः तीन वर्ष का होगा:-- 
(क) जो संसद सदस्य समिति के सदस्य हैं वे संसद सदस्य न रहने पर इस समिति के सदस्य नहीं रहेंगे। 

(ख) समिति के पदेन सदस्य अपने पद पर कार्य करते रहने तक ही समिति के सदस्य होंगे।

IL. Functions 


The functions of the Committee will be to advise on the implementation of the provisions relating to the official 
language in the Constitution, the Official Languages Act and Rules, the decisions of the Central Hindi Committee and the 
directions/instructions issued by the Department of Official Language and to promote the progressive use of Hindi in the 
functioning of the Ministry of External Affairs. 


Ill. Tenure 


The tenure of the Committee shall ordinarily be three years from the date of constitution of the Committee, subject to 
the following:— 


(a) Members of Parliament who are members of the Committee shall cease to be members of this Committee 
if they cease to be members of Parliament. 


(b)  (b) Ex-officio members of the Committee shall be members of the Committee as long as they hold their 
office. 


(c) The member nominated on the vacancy caused due to death of any member or resignation from the membership 
of the committee will be a member only for the remaining period of the tenure of the committee. 


(d) Ifa person is nominated as a member of the committee during the tenure of the committee, then he will be a 
member only for the remaining period of the tenure of the committee. 


(e) Under special circumstances, the tenure of the committee can be reduced or extended by the Ministry with the 
consent of the Department of Official Language. 


IV. General 


The headquarters of Committee will be in New Delhi, but the Committee can hold its meetings at any other place if 
necessary. 


V. Travelling Allowance and other Allowances 


(a) Under the Department of Official Language's OM No. 11/20034/04/2005-OL. (Pol-2) dated 03 February, 2006, 
the Members of Parliament nominated to the Committee shall be paid travelling Allowance/daily Allowance for attending the 
meetings of the Committee as per the provisions of the "Members of Parliament (Salaries, Allowances and Pension) Act, 1954" 
and the amendments issued from time to time and the rules made thereunder. (b) In view of the highlevel nature of this 
Committee, the non-official members of the Committee shall be paid Travelling Allowance/ Daily Allowance as per the 
guidelines contained in the Department of Official Language's OM No. 11 / 20034 /4/86- OL (A-2) dated 22 January, 1987 and 
as per the rates and rules as amended / fixed by the Government of India from time to time. 


ORDER 


ORDERED that a copy of this Resolution be sent to all the members of the Committee, all State Governments and 
Union Territory Administrations, the President's Secretariat, the Vice President's Secretariat, the Prime Minister's Office, the 
Cabinet Secretariat, the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Lok Sabha Secretariat, Rajya Sabha Secretariat, NITI Aayog, the 
Comptroller and Auditor General of India, the Accountant General, Central Revenue and all the Ministries and Departments 
of the Government of India. 


It is also ordered that this Resolution be published in the Gazette of India for general information.
